blocks.content:
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable.
• Courts may use them to interpret laws.
• Violation may attract penalties under specific laws.

items: Remember that Fundamental Duties lack direct legal enforceability (non-justiciable nature).
Parliament has the power to enforce specific Fundamental Duties by creating legal penalties through individual enactments.
Courts can consider Fundamental Duties while determining the reasonableness of restrictions on Fundamental Rights.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and cannot be directly enforced by courts of law.
Courts may utilize Fundamental Duties as an interpretive tool to examine the constitutionality and meaning of laws.
Direct violation does not carry automatic legal sanction, but Parliament may enact specific laws prescribing penalties.
